subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which two structures make up the mammalian central nervous system (CNS)?
options: The brain and the spinal cord
The brain and the sensory neurones
The spinal cord and the effectors
The nerves and the receptors
questions.explain: The CNS consists of the brain and spinal cord, which coordinate the body's responses.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of a reflex arc?
options: Stimulus → receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector
Stimulus → motor neurone → relay neurone → sensory neurone → receptor → effector
Receptor → stimulus → motor neurone → effector → sensory neurone → relay neurone
Stimulus → effector → motor neurone → relay neurone → sensory neurone → receptor
questions.explain: Impulses pass from a receptor through sensory, relay and motor neurones to an effector that carries out the response.

questions.q: How is a nerve impulse transmitted across a synapse?
options: A neurotransmitter chemical diffuses across the gap and binds to receptors on the next neurone
An electrical current jumps directly across the gap between the neurones
The two neurones fuse together so the impulse passes through
Blood carries the impulse from one neurone to the next
questions.explain: At a synapse a chemical neurotransmitter is released, diffuses across the gap and triggers an impulse in the next neurone.

questions.q: What name is given to the junction between two neurones?
options: A synapse
A reflex arc
An effector
A receptor
questions.explain: A synapse is the small gap between the ends of two adjacent neurones.

questions.q: Why is a reflex action described as rapid and automatic?
options: It does not require processing by the conscious parts of the brain
It is controlled entirely by hormones in the blood
It always involves only one neurone
It can be prevented by conscious thought
questions.explain: A reflex action is an involuntary response that bypasses conscious brain processing, making it fast and protective.

questions.q: A sense organ is best defined as:
options: A group of receptor cells responding to a specific stimulus
A group of muscle cells that bring about a response
A gland that releases hormones into the blood
A bundle of motor neurones carrying impulses to effectors
questions.explain: Sense organs contain groups of receptor cells that detect specific stimuli such as light, sound or chemicals.

questions.q: Which part of the eye carries out most of the refraction (bending) of light entering it?
options: The cornea
The retina
The optic nerve
The iris
questions.explain: The transparent cornea refracts most of the light entering the eye, with the lens providing fine focusing.

questions.q: In bright light, how does the iris adjust the pupil?
options: The circular muscles contract and the radial muscles relax, making the pupil smaller
The radial muscles contract and the circular muscles relax, making the pupil smaller
The circular muscles contract and the radial muscles relax, making the pupil larger
Both sets of muscles relax so the pupil stays the same size
questions.explain: In bright light the circular muscles contract to constrict the pupil, reducing the light reaching the retina.

questions.q: A student switches from reading a book to looking at a distant tree. How does the lens change to focus on the distant object?
options: The ciliary muscles relax, the suspensory ligaments tighten and the lens becomes thinner
The ciliary muscles contract, the suspensory ligaments slacken and the lens becomes thicker
The ciliary muscles relax, the suspensory ligaments slacken and the lens becomes thicker
The ciliary muscles contract, the suspensory ligaments tighten and the lens becomes thinner
questions.explain: For distant objects the ciliary muscles relax, tightening the suspensory ligaments and pulling the lens thin.

questions.q: Which light receptor cells of the retina are responsible for detecting colour?
options: Cones
Rods
Relay cells
Ciliary cells
questions.explain: Cone cells in the retina are sensitive to colour, whereas rods detect dim light and only shades of grey.

questions.q: Which statement best defines a hormone?
options: A chemical substance, produced by a gland, carried by the blood, that alters the activity of one or more target organs
A chemical released at a synapse to pass an impulse between neurones
A protein made by muscle cells to bring about movement
An electrical signal carried along a neurone to an effector
questions.explain: Hormones are chemical messengers made by endocrine glands and transported in the blood to target organs.

questions.q: Which gland produces the hormone adrenaline?
options: The adrenal glands
The pancreas
The pituitary gland
The salivary glands
questions.explain: Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal glands, which sit above the kidneys.

questions.q: Which set of changes is brought about by the release of adrenaline?
options: Increased heart rate and increased breathing rate
Decreased heart rate and decreased breathing rate
Lowered blood glucose and increased urine production
Constriction of the pupils and slowed reactions
questions.explain: Adrenaline prepares the body for 'fight or flight', raising heart and breathing rates to deliver more oxygen and glucose.

questions.q: Compared with nervous control, hormonal (chemical) control of the body is generally:
options: Slower to act but longer lasting in its effect
Faster to act and shorter lasting in its effect
Faster to act and longer lasting in its effect
Slower to act and shorter lasting in its effect
questions.explain: Hormones travel in the blood so act more slowly than nerve impulses, but their effects last longer.

questions.q: What does the term homeostasis mean?
options: The maintenance of a constant internal environment
The response of a plant towards light
The transmission of impulses across a synapse
The detection of stimuli by sense organs
questions.explain: Homeostasis is the control of internal conditions, such as temperature and blood glucose, within set limits.

questions.q: How does insulin help to control blood glucose concentration?
options: It stimulates the liver to convert excess glucose into glycogen, lowering blood glucose
It stimulates the liver to convert glycogen into glucose, raising blood glucose
It increases the breakdown of proteins to release glucose
It causes glucose to be removed from the body in sweat
questions.explain: Insulin from the pancreas lowers blood glucose by promoting its conversion to glycogen for storage in the liver.

questions.q: A person becomes very hot after exercise. Which combination of skin responses helps to cool them down?
options: Sweating increases and blood vessels near the skin surface widen (vasodilation)
Sweating decreases and blood vessels near the skin surface narrow (vasoconstriction)
Sweating increases and blood vessels near the skin surface narrow (vasoconstriction)
Shivering begins and hairs stand upright to trap air
questions.explain: When overheated, vasodilation and increased sweating both increase heat loss from the skin to cool the body.

questions.q: After a sugary meal, a person's blood glucose rises sharply and then returns to normal. This return to normal is an example of:
options: Negative feedback correcting a change away from the set level
Positive feedback amplifying the change further
A reflex arc controlled by the spinal cord
A tropic response of the body to food
questions.explain: A rise in glucose triggers insulin release that brings the level back down, which is negative feedback control.

questions.q: What is phototropism?
options: A growth response of a plant in which the direction of growth is determined by the direction of light
A growth response of a plant to the direction of gravity
The movement of a whole plant towards water
The response of an animal to a change in temperature
questions.explain: Phototropism is a directional growth response to light; shoots grow towards light (positively phototropic).

questions.q: A shoot is lit from one side only and bends towards the light. How does the hormone auxin cause this?
options: Auxin gathers on the shaded side, making those cells elongate more so the shoot bends towards the light
Auxin gathers on the lit side, making those cells elongate more so the shoot bends towards the light
Auxin is destroyed on the shaded side, so that side grows less
Auxin prevents all growth on the shaded side so the shoot bends away from the light
questions.explain: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side, causing greater cell elongation there so the shoot bends towards the light.
